'''Roger Sidney Goody''' (born 17 April 1944, in [[Northampton]]) is an English [[chemist]] who served as director at the [[Max Planck Institute for Molecular Physiology]] in [[Dortmund]] from 1993 until 2013.<ref name=mpi>{{cite web |url=http://www.mpi-dortmund.mpg.de/english/ueberInstitut/Struktur/Direktoren/Goody/index.html |title=Max Planck Institute of Molecular Physiology, Dortmund - Prof. Dr. Roger S. Goody |website=www.mpi-dortmund.mpg.de |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070610175942/http://www.mpi-dortmund.mpg.de/english/ueberInstitut/Struktur/Direktoren/Goody/index.html |archive-date=2007-06-10}}</ref> Since 2013 he is Emeritus Director of the institute.

== Education ==
Goody studied Chemistry at the [[University of Birmingham]], England, where he was awarded a [[PhD]] in 1968 for 
studies on the chemistry of [[cytosine]].<ref name=phd>{{cite thesis|degree=PhD|publisher=University of Birmingham|first=Roger Sidney|last=Goody|year=1968| url=http://www.findit.bham.ac.uk/44BIR_VU1:CSCOP_44BIR_DEEP:44BIR_ALEPH_DS003266465|id={{Copac|45170305}}|website=bham.ac.uk|title=Studies on the chemistry of cytosine and its derivatives|oclc=911166913 }}</ref>

==Career and research==
After his PhD, Goody was appointed a [[postdoctoral researcher]] at the [[Memorial Sloan-Kettering Cancer Center]] in [[New York City]], NY, USA in the field of [[natural products]] research. In 1970 he became a scientific fellow at the [[Max Planck Institute for Experimental Medicine]], Göttingen in the field of [[nucleotide]] research. From 1972 till 1993 he was a group leader at the [[Max Planck Institute for Medical Research]], Heidelberg in the field of [[enzymology]] and [[nucleotide]] research, with a focus on [[actin]], [[myosin]], [[adenylate kinase]], [[EF-Tu]], [[HRAS]]-p21, [[reverse transcriptase]], [[nucleotides]] and [[nucleic acid]] sequencing. An overriding theme of his research interests has been the transient states of enzymes, along the enzyme reaction pathway, against the background of selective and specific ligand-protein interactions and structure-function relationships. In 1983 he habilitated at the faculty for biochemistry and biophysics of the University of Heidelberg and was announced adjunct professor in 1990. In 1993 he accepted the position of Director at the [[Max Planck Institute for Molecular Physiology]], Dortmund and became a scientific fellow of the [[Max Planck Society]].<ref name=mpi/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mpg.de/424930/molekulare_physiologie_wissM|title=Goody, Roger S|website=www.mpg.de}}</ref> Since 2004 he has also held a full professorship in biochemistry (supramolecular systems) at the [[Ruhr University Bochum]], with a dual emphasis on higher education and fundamental research.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.uv.ruhr-uni-bochum.de/pvz-planung/i3v/00032900/03882222.htm|title=Vorlesungsverzeichnis SS 2018|website=www.uv.ruhr-uni-bochum.de}}</ref>

Goody has combined chemistry, structural biology and kinetics to make major contributions in several fields of biology. He pioneered the use of nucleotide analogs, synthesized at the beginning of his career, in muscle research and later for Ras-family GTPases, leading to the first ever structure determination of an unstable protein-substrate complex (Ras:GTP). Innovative use of semi-synthetic proteins led to an understanding of transport mechanisms of [[Rab (G-protein)|Rab GTPases]] and to resolution of a longstanding controversy concerning targeting of these proteins to membranes. His group discovered and characterized hitherto unrecognized covalent modifications of Rab proteins by bacteria.

=== Honours, awards and memberships ===
From 2013 to 2015, Goody was President of the German Society for Biochemistry and molecular Biology (GBM).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gbm-online.de/gremien.html|title=GBM-Startseite - Homepage der Gesellschaft für Biochemie und Molekularbiologie e.V|website=www.gbm-online.de}}</ref> In 2018 he was elected Fellow of the [[Royal Society]].

* President of the German Society of Biochemistry and molecular Biology
* German Academy of Sciences Leopoldina (since 2003)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.leopoldina.org/mitglieder/mitgliederverzeichnis/member/969/|title = Mitglieder}}</ref>
* Max Bergman Society{{citation needed|date=May 2018}}
* Awarded membership of the [[European Molecular Biology Organization]] (EMBO)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://people.embo.org/profile/roger-s-goody|title=Find people in the EMBO Communities|website=people.embo.org}}</ref>
* Member of the Scientific Advisory Board of the [[Max Delbrück Center for Molecular Medicine]] (MDC) Berlin Buch
* Chairman of the Study Section for Biochemistry, Biophysics and Structural Biology of the [[Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft]] (German National Research Organization) - 2000-2009
*1991: Max Planck Prize{{citation needed|date=May 2018}}
*2003: [[German Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://websrv.leopoldina.org/en/members/list-of-members/member/969/|title=List of Members|website=websrv.leopoldina.org}}</ref>
*2008: Max Bergmann Medal<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.max-bergmann-kreis.org/preis_mbm.html|title=Max Bergmann Kreis}}</ref>

*2012: Xu Guangqi Lecture,  CAS-Max-Planck Partner Institute, Shanghai China
*2015: [[Feldberg Prize]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.feldbergfoundation.org/prizewinners/|title = Prizewinners &#124; Feldberg Foundation}}</ref>
*2018: Elected [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] (FRS)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/news/2018/05/distinguished-scientists-elected-fellows-royal-society-2018/|title=Distinguished scientists elected as Fellows and Foreign Members of the Royal Society|website=royalsociety.org}}</ref>
*2024: [[Cothenius Medal]]<ref>{{cite news |last1=Jarzombek |first1=Johann |title=Renowned Cothenius Medal for Max Planck scientist Roger Sidney Goody |url=https://www.mpi-dortmund.mpg.de/news/roger-goody-leopoldina-cothenius-medal |access-date=8 July 2025 |agency=Max Planck Institute of Molecular Biology |issue=Max-Planck-Gesellschaft |date=23 August 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250708094845/https://www.mpi-dortmund.mpg.de/news/roger-goody-leopoldina-cothenius-medal|archive-date=8 July 2025}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Goody is married to the biologist Dr. Waltraud Hofmann-Goody and has two children.{{citation needed|date=May 2018}}
